verdict: The exact M798 command consumed its only canonical attempt and then failed deterministically before staging allocation or any decoder schedule row. The runner-created hierarchical attempt seal is incompatible with the frozen generic sealed-population verifier. No cycle, speedup, decoder-complete or Table-A claim exists. The M798 identity must never be rerun; only a new additive identity may repair the boundary.

attempt_identity.reason: The runner refuses any existing canonical attempt before production and the true release authorizes max_attempts=1. Deleting, moving or rewriting the sentinel would violate the one-shot contract.

failure_localization.explanation: The runner intentionally placed attempt.json under initial/ and made the root manifest name only initial/SHA256SUMS.seal.sha256. The generic verifier recursively counts every non-root-seal file, so the nested initial/SHA256SUMS and initial/attempt.json are deterministic unexpected members. The exact canonical attempt path is passed throughout; no unrelated file was injected.

execution_boundary.reason: The failing attempt verification precedes output.mkdir, contract loading, oracle loading and all record/timestep/config schedule loops.

runner_failure_receipt_audit.current_behavior: The EXIT trap has only published-result and existing-stage branches; if both are absent it exits without a failed_or_incomplete artifact.
runner_failure_receipt_audit.required_repair: After one-shot consumption, every nonzero exit must atomically publish a double-sealed failure receipt even when no stage was created. The receipt must bind rc, attempt outer seal, candidate/driver/runner/release SHA values and phase flags, without presenting cycles.

findings.finding: The exact runner creates an attempt population that its exact production driver deterministically rejects only after the one-shot has been irreversibly consumed.
The post-consumption EXIT trap emits no sealed failed_or_incomplete receipt when validation fails before stage creation, leaving terminal output as the only direct failure record.

repair_steps: Use a flat attempt population whose root SHA256SUMS directly names attempt.json, or introduce one exact hierarchical-seal verifier and test it against the runner-created byte-exact attempt tree. Do not mix the two formats.

Before release, construct the exact future attempt tree in a temporary sibling and execute the full attempt-required validation path; require it to reach the boundary immediately before staging allocation without scheduling rows.
Make the runner publish an atomic no-clobber, double-sealed failure receipt on every post-consumption nonzero exit, including failures before stage creation.

Bind the new candidate, driver, runner, tests, canonical paths and failure-receipt schema by exact SHA; obtain a fresh source hammer, author a new true release, then obtain a fresh final launch hammer before one production replay.

next_authorization.required_next_gate: Fresh source hammer of the new byte-exact attempt-layout and failure-receipt closure; only after PASS may a separate new true release and final launch hammer be created.
